sasonr

Execute SAS programs on an R engine.

sasonr is an independent implementation of SAS 9.4 program semantics in R, written with reference to the publicly available SAS 9.4 documentation. Features it does not support fail loud instead of being approximated. Compatibility with SAS is not guaranteed. sasonr is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by SAS Institute Inc. SAS is a registered trademark of SAS Institute Inc.

sasonr parses SAS source code (DATA step, macro language, PROC SQL and a growing set of procedures) into an abstract syntax tree with a hand-written lexer, recursive-descent parser and Pratt expression parser, then executes it in R: DATA steps are compiled into tidyverse code, PROC SQL runs on DuckDB.

Three ways to use it:

  1. SAS programs in R - execute SAS programs in an R session.
  2. Deterministic SAS to R migration - sas_translate() produces R code without any language model.
  3. R / SAS double programming - one programmer writes R, the other writes SAS code and runs it with sasonr on the same platform.

Design rules:

  • Deterministic: no language model is involved at run time.
  • Fail loud: a language feature that sasonr does not support raises a sasonr_unsupported condition with the SAS line number instead of guessing.

Status: early development, not on CRAN.

# pak::pak("kaipingyang/sasonr")
library(sasonr)
res <- sas_run("data a; do i = 1 to 3; x = i**2; output; end; run;")
sas_log(res)                                      # the log, with the program lines
sas_translate("data b; set a; if x > 1; run;")   # show generated R code
